record.original_question: Assume the positive relation \( inom{d}{\omega} 	o  inom{d}{\omega}^{1,1}_2\) holds. After adding λ many random reals for some λ > d, must that same positive relation for d and ω still hold?

evidence.quote: Problem 2.9. Assume (d over ω) → (d over ω)^(1,1)_2, and one adds λ-many random reals (for some λ > d). Does the positive relation (d over ω) → (d over ω)^(1,1)_2 still holds?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Notation. For infinite cardinals $\kappa$ and $\lambda$, the strong polarized partition relation $\binom{\kappa}{\lambda} \to \binom{\kappa}{\lambda}^{1,1}_{2}$ asserts that for every coloring $c\colon \kappa \times \lambda \to \{0,1\}$ there exist $A \subseteq \kappa$ with $|A| = \kappa$ and $B \subseteq \lambda$ with $|B| = \lambda$ such that $c \restriction (A \times B)$ is constant. Let $\mathfrak{d}$ denote the dominating number, i.e. the least cardinality of a family $D \subseteq {}^{\omega}\omega$ such that every $f \in {}^{\omega}\omega$ is eventually dominated by some member of $D$.

Problem. Work in a model of ZFC in which the strong polarized relation
$$\binom{\mathfrak{d}}{\omega} \to \binom{\mathfrak{d}}{\omega}^{1,1}_{2}$$
holds. Let $\lambda$ be a cardinal with $\lambda > \mathfrak{d}$, and force with the measure algebra adding $\lambda$ many random reals. Must the strong polarized relation $\binom{\mathfrak{d}}{\omega} \to \binom{\mathfrak{d}}{\omega}^{1,1}_{2}$ continue to hold in the generic extension (where $\mathfrak{d}$ is computed in the extension)?
artifact.status_search_result: A subsequent 2018 paper by Garti and Shelah, "Random reals and polarized colorings" (Studia Sci. Math. Hungar. 55(2), 203–212), explicitly studies the effect of adding random reals on strong polarized partition relations involving cardinal characteristics of the continuum, showing that random real forcing tends to produce negative polarized relations. This addresses Problem 2.9, with the answer in the negative direction in the cases analyzed there, although a fully general resolution for all models is not clearly stated in publicly available abstracts.

status_evidence.title: Random reals and polarized colorings — Studia Sci. Math. Hungar. 55 (2018)
status_evidence.snippet: Random reals (as well as the existence of real-valued measurable cardinals) yield downward negative polarized relations.
status_evidence.claim: Garti and Shelah show that adding random reals destroys strong polarized partition relations of the relevant form, addressing the preservation question for d and ω.

status_evidence.title: Garti–Shelah, Random reals and polarized colorings (PDF)
status_evidence.snippet: Analysis of strong polarized partition relations under random real forcing; random reals do not preserve such positive relations in general.
status_evidence.claim: Follow-up work by the same authors directly examines the polarized partition relation under random real forcing.
